openaiSpec.name: render_interactive_canvas

htmlSource.description: The full HTML source to render to the canvas. Must be a complete document (e.g. starting with <!DOCTYPE html> or <html>). After this initial render, prefer the `update_interactive_canvas` tool to make small edits — it is much faster and uses far fewer tokens than re-emitting the entire HTML.

canvasHeight.description: The height of the canvas in pixels. Default is 500.

openaiSpec.description: Render an interactive canvas with HTML source to the user interface. The HTML source can include JavaScript and CSS to create interactive elements. This can be used to create custom user interfaces, games, demos, charts, and more. The canvas width is always 100% of the container width, and the height can be specified in pixels. Use this for the FIRST render and for full rewrites. For small follow-up tweaks to a canvas you have already rendered, prefer `update_interactive_canvas`.

pluginFunctions.name: Update Interactive Canvas

openaiSpec.name: update_interactive_canvas

edits.description: An ordered list of search-and-replace edits to apply to the most recently rendered interactive canvas HTML. Edits are applied sequentially: each edit operates on the result of the previous one. Each `oldText` must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the current HTML — include enough surrounding context (whitespace and neighbouring tags) to make the match unique. To insert new content, set `oldText` to a unique anchor that already exists and put both that anchor and the new content into `newText`. To delete content, set `newText` to an empty string.

oldText.description: The exact substring to find in the current HTML. Whitespace, casing and punctuation must match byte-for-byte. Must occur exactly once in the current HTML.

newText.description: The replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the matched region.

openaiSpec.description:
Apply small, targeted edits to the most recently rendered interactive canvas instead of re-emitting the full HTML. Each edit performs an exact, literal find-and-replace on the current HTML. Use this WHENEVER you only need to tweak parts of an existing canvas you previously rendered with `render_interactive_canvas` — it is much faster and uses far fewer output tokens than re-emitting the entire HTML.

Rules:
- Do NOT use this for the very first render — use `render_interactive_canvas` instead.
- Each `oldText` must match EXACTLY ONCE in the current HTML; include enough surrounding context to make it unique. If a match is ambiguous (matches more than once) or missing, the call will fail and you should retry with more context, or fall back to `render_interactive_canvas` with the full updated HTML.
- Edits are applied in order; later edits see the result of earlier ones.
- Prefer many small edits over one big rewrite — it makes failures localised and easier to retry.
